charts.name: Sierra Leone reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: There is no legal chart of accounts in Sierra Leone. IFRS Standards are required of listed companies, banks and insurers, and IFRS for SMEs, adopted by CSAAG resolution BPR2/2009 under authority delegated by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sierra Leone (ICASL), is permitted for the other entities. This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of the IFRS-based statements below, with the accounts a Sierra Leonean company actually keeps — GST input and output tax, import GST owed to the National Revenue Authority at the border, NASSIT contributions, PAYE, payroll tax, withholding tax, the 2 per cent tourism levy and excise duty payable, and the irrecoverable GST that the Act leaves with a buyer.

numbering.legal_reference: Goods and Services Tax Act, 2009, s. 31 and the Authority's page on GST invoices — a GST invoice carries the number of the invoice taken from a consecutive series, and s. 34 as replaced by the Finance Act 2020 makes the invoice or the electronic cash register receipt the document of record. A consecutive series is what the text asks for; whether it must be without gap is not stated, which is why `numbering` is `sequential` and not `gapless_per_year`.

tax_point.legal_reference: Goods and Services Tax Act, 2009, Part IV (time of supply, s. 19): the supply is made at the earliest of the events the Act lists — delivery or making available, payment, invoice. Ekwo's closed vocabulary expresses a two-way earliest test; `earliest_of_delivery_or_payment` is the nearest value and the gap — an invoice issued ahead of both delivery and payment — is written in this pack's README.

einvoicing.legal_reference: No Sierra Leonean statute obliges a business to exchange a structured electronic invoice with another business in the sense Ekwo's vocabulary gives the word: there is no Peppol authority, no published profile and no scheme a party is addressed by, so `profile`, `party_scheme` and `vat_scheme` are null and `obligation` is `none`. What Sierra Leone has instead is the electronic cash register: s. 34 of the GST Act, replaced by s. 34 of the Finance Act 2020, requires every GST-registered business to keep an electronic cash register specified by the Commissioner-General, made of a Certified Invoicing System and a Sales Data Controller that signs each receipt and sends it to the Authority's server. That is fiscal-device reporting to the tax administration and not a peer-to-peer exchange; the gap is recorded in this pack's README and the core is not patched to fit it.
